primary_source_citation.title: SME Surface Open-Pit vs Underground Mining Standard Technical Reference

bespoke_clusters.rule_of_thumb_mnemonic: Surface mining (open-pit, strip, and quarry) is chosen when the stripping ratio of waste overburden to shallow ore is economically low.
core_mechanism_bullets: Surface mining (open-pit, strip, and quarry) is chosen when the stripping ratio of waste overburden to shallow ore is economically low.
Underground mining (room-and-pillar, longwall, and block caving) accesses deep seams via shafts or declines supported by roof bolts.
bespoke_clusters.worked_field_example: If an ore seam 10 feet thick lies beneath 60 feet of waste rock, the overburden stripping ratio is 6 to 1, favoring surface strip mining rather than deep vertical shaft sinking.
